item.title: Xi and Putin hail ties in video call as Ukraine war nears anniversary
item.description:
Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin celebrated their nations' partnership during a video call on Wednesday, with both leaders signaling a commitment to deepen strategic cooperation as the fourth anniversary of Russia's invasion of Ukraine approaches later this month.

In remarks broadcast on Russian state television, Putin described the Moscow-Beijing relationship as a "stabilizing factor" amid global turbulence, while Xi called for a "grand plan" to advance bilateral ties that he said were on the "right trajectory."

item.title: Oil prices stabilize as Iran agrees to nuclear talks with US
item.description:
Crude oil prices have climbed over the past month, driven by escalating tensions between the United States and Iran that threaten global energy supplies, while falling inventories and winter weather disruptions have added further support to the market.

WTI crude oil rose on Tuesday, continuing a rally that has lifted prices more than 9% over the past month, according to Trading Economics. Brent crude gained in early Tuesday trading, with MUFG research analyst Soojin Kim noting that market focus remains on the Strait of Hormuz, "a critical chokepoint for global oil and liquified gas flows".

item.title: Donors withhold Gaza reconstruction funds over Hamas disarmament
item.description:
International backers are declining to commit funds to the Trump administration's Gaza reconstruction initiative as negotiations over Hamas disarmament have stalled, leaving the devastated territory's more than two million residents unable to begin rebuilding, according to sources familiar with the matter.

The United States has yet to secure financial commitments for its reconstruction plan, with potential donors expressing concern that the impasse over disarmament could lead Israel to resume large-scale military operations in Gaza, sources told Reuters on Tuesday. Seven Western diplomats confirmed the funding delay, which has not been previously reported, noting that some prospective contributors are also requesting that funds be managed by the United Nations rather than by President Donald Trump's Board of Peace.

item.title: Russia's budget deficit may triple as oil revenues plunge
item.description:
Russia's budget deficit could swell to nearly three times the government's official target by the end of 2026, according to leaked calculations from a government-linked think tank cited by Reuters, as Western sanctions and declining oil prices continue to squeeze the Kremlin's finances.

The Finance Ministry's data released Tuesday showed oil and gas revenues in January fell by half compared to the same month a year earlier, dropping to 393.6 billion rubles ($5.1 billion), the lowest level since July 2020 during the COVID-19 pandemic. The collapse underscores the mounting pressure on Moscow's fiscal position as it funds the ongoing war in Ukraine.

item.title: Russian satellites suspected of intercepting European communications
item.description:
Russian reconnaissance satellites have intercepted communications from at least a dozen critical European satellites over the past three years, jeopardizing the confidentiality of sensitive government and military data transmitted across the continent, according to European security officials.

The Financial Times reported on February 4 that two Russian spacecraft, Luch-1 and Luch-2, have conducted prolonged proximity operations near key European geostationary satellites that serve the continent, including the United Kingdom, as well as portions of Africa and the Middle East. Since its launch in 2023, Luch-2 alone has approached at least 17 European satellites, many of which are operated by NATO-affiliated entities.

item.title: Global markets rebound after AI-driven software stock rout
item.description: Wall Street futures pointed higher Wednesday morning as global markets steadied following a steep sell-off in software and data stocks that erased roughly $300 billion in market value over the previous session. The rout, triggered by new artificial intelligence automation tools from Anthropic, raised investor fears that AI platforms could become direct competitors to legacy software providers.

item.title: IOC considers moving Winter Olympics to January amid climate concerns
item.description:
Days before the Opening Ceremony of the 2026 Winter Olympics in Italy, the International Olympic Committee signaled it is considering moving future Winter Games from February to January as rising global temperatures threaten the long-term viability of the snow-dependent event.

Karl Stoss, IOC member in charge of the sports program evaluation, said Wednesday that shifting the Games earlier could help secure more reliable snow conditions. "Perhaps we are also contemplating moving the Winter Olympics to an earlier date," Stoss told reporters at an IOC pre-Olympics gathering in Milan, noting this would also affect Paralympic scheduling. The Paralympics, currently set for March, could shift to February under the proposal.

item.title: Gold surges after US downs Iranian drone near aircraft carrier
item.description:
Gold prices rallied sharply in early February 2026 after renewed tensions between the United States and Iran sent investors seeking refuge in safe-haven assets. On Wednesday, spot gold rose above $5,040 per ounce, extending its biggest single-day gain since November 2008, as geopolitical risks intensified in the Persian Gulf region.

The precious metal has recovered sharply from a steep selloff that saw prices tumble to around $4,400 on Monday, with Tuesday's 5.9% surge marking the largest daily increase in nearly two decades. The rebound comes as diplomatic efforts between Washington and Tehran have faltered and military confrontations have escalated.

item.title: Binance founder loses faith in 2026 'super cycle' as Bitcoin tumbles
item.description:
Famed "Big Short" investor Michael Burry is sounding the alarm on what he calls "sickening scenarios" that could unfold if Bitcoin continues its months-long slide, warning that corporate treasuries and crypto miners face catastrophic losses that could ripple through traditional markets.

In a Substack post published Monday, Burry argued that the original cryptocurrency has been exposed as a purely speculative asset, failing to establish itself as a hedge against currency devaluation similar to precious metals. The warning comes as Bitcoin has tumbled more than 40% from its October 2025 peak above $126,000, briefly falling below $73,000 this week before recovering slightly.

item.title: Syria signs offshore oil deal with Chevron and Qatari firm
item.description:
Syria's state-run petroleum company signed a memorandum of understanding with Chevron and Qatar-based Power International Holding on Wednesday to explore for oil and gas in Syrian territorial waters, marking the country's first formal step toward offshore energy development.

The agreement was signed in Damascus in the presence of U.S. Special Envoy for Syria Tom Barrack, who praised the deal as "a transformative step toward reshaping Syria's image after years of hardship."

item.title: Iran moves to reshape nuclear talks as Gulf provocations rise
item.description:
Iran has upended planned multi-party nuclear negotiations while simultaneously launching military provocations in the Persian Gulf, in what analysts describe as a coordinated effort to reshape the dynamics of looming talks with the United States.

On Feb. 3, Tehran demanded that Friday's planned talks be moved from Istanbul to Oman and shifted from a multilateral format to strictly bilateral negotiations focused only on its nuclear program, according to sources cited by Axios and Bloomberg. The maneuver represents a sharp reversal from understandings reached in recent days, after several regional powers had already been invited to participate in the Istanbul meeting.

item.title: Amazon to launch AI tools for film and TV production in March
item.description:
Amazon has announced plans to use artificial intelligence to accelerate and reduce the cost of movie and television production, even as concerns persist throughout Hollywood about the technology's potential to eliminate jobs and fundamentally transform the entertainment industry.

At Amazon MGM Studios, veteran entertainment executive Albert Cheng is leading a team developing new AI tools designed to cut costs and streamline the creative process. The company plans to launch a closed beta program in March, inviting industry partners to test the tools, with results expected by May.

item.title: Xi holds back-to-back calls with Putin, Trump as nuclear pact expires
item.description:
Chinese President Xi Jinping engaged in a diplomatic double-header on Wednesday, holding a video conference with Russian President Vladimir Putin before speaking by phone with U.S. President Donald Trump, as the last remaining nuclear arms control agreement between Washington and Moscow is set to expire on Thursday.

The conversations came one day before the New Strategic Arms Reduction Treaty (New START) lapses, potentially marking the first time since the early 1970s that U.S. and Russian strategic nuclear forces will operate without legally binding constraints.

item.title: Ozone-saving chemicals linked to 335,000 tonnes of forever chemical pollution
item.description:
A new study has found that chemicals introduced to protect the ozone layer have caused hundreds of thousands of tonnes of a persistent "forever chemical" to spread across the planet, from rainwater and drinking water to Arctic ice.

Research led by Lancaster University and published in the journal Geophysical Research Letters on February 4 calculated that chlorofluorocarbon (CFC) replacement chemicals and inhalation anesthetics deposited approximately 335,500 metric tonnes of trifluoroacetic acid (TFA) across Earth's surface between 2000 and 2022. The rate of TFA entering the environment continues to grow, with peak annual production from these sources estimated to occur anywhere between 2025 and 2100.

item.title: X4.2 solar flare triggers radio blackouts across Africa, Europe
item.description:
The sun erupted with a major X4.2-class solar flare on Tuesday, the latest in a week-long barrage of explosive activity that has space weather experts watching closely for possible aurora displays and radio disruptions on Earth.

The flare, which peaked at 12:13 UTC on February 4, originated from Active Region 4366, an enormous and magnetically complex sunspot that scientists have dubbed a "solar flare factory." The eruption triggered strong radio blackouts across parts of Africa and Europe, where high-frequency communications were temporarily disrupted.

item.title: US-Iran nuclear talks collapse over scope and location dispute
item.description:
Scheduled nuclear negotiations between the United States and Iran fell apart Wednesday after Washington rejected Tehran's last-minute demands to move the talks from Istanbul to Oman and narrow their scope exclusively to nuclear issues, U.S. officials told Axios on February 4, 2026.

The breakdown came after Iran walked back previous agreements by insisting the Friday meeting take place in the Gulf state rather than Turkey, while also pushing for a purely bilateral format that would exclude discussions on ballistic missiles, regional proxies, and human rights.

"We told them it is this or nothing, and they said, 'Ok, then nothing,'" a senior U.S. official told Axios.

item.title: Study finds over 2,500 non-native plants could survive in Arctic
item.description:
A new study has identified more than 2,500 plant species that could potentially survive and establish themselves in the Arctic today, raising alarm about a looming ecological threat to one of Earth's most vulnerable ecosystems.

The research, published in the journal NeoBiota, found that 2,554 alien vascular plant species could find a suitable climatic niche in the Arctic tundra if transported there, with northern Norway emerging as a primary hotspot for potential invasions.

item.title: Saudi Arabia, Turkey sign deal for 5,000 MW of solar projects
item.description: Turkey and Saudi Arabia announced a sweeping expansion of economic and energy cooperation on Tuesday following Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan's official visit to Riyadh, where he met with Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman at Al-Yamamah Palace. The two countries issued a joint statement pledging to raise bilateral trade from its current level of more than $8.6 billion to $10 billion in the short term and $30 billion over the long term, while signing agreements to develop renewable energy projects and strengthen defense ties.

item.title: Oil prices surge as U.S.-Iran nuclear talks collapse
item.description:
Oil prices jumped more than 3% on Wednesday after reports emerged that planned nuclear talks between the United States and Iran have collapsed, reigniting fears of military conflict in the Middle East and potential disruptions to global oil supplies.

U.S. crude oil rose roughly 3.5% while global benchmark Brent climbed about 3.4% in afternoon trading, according to Investing.com. The sharp gains came after Axios reported that negotiations scheduled for Friday had been effectively canceled following a dispute over the location and scope of the discussions.

item.title: US-Iran nuclear talks back on after Arab leaders lobby Trump
item.description:
Scheduled nuclear negotiations between the United States and Iran appeared on the verge of collapse Wednesday before urgent appeals from at least nine Middle Eastern nations convinced the Trump administration to proceed with talks in Oman on Friday.

The diplomatic whiplash came after Iran demanded changes to both the venue and format of the meeting, initially planned for Istanbul. Tehran requested the talks be moved to Muscat and narrowed to a strictly bilateral format focused exclusively on nuclear issues, excluding discussions of ballistic missiles and regional proxy networks that Washington had sought to include.
